Issued at 310 PM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

Afternoon RAP analysis continues to depict broad upper level ridging 
extending from the central CONUS into southern Manitoba and 
northwest Ontario, however there is some evidence of an impending 
pattern change as a deep upper level trough begins to lift out of 
the Pacific Northwest. Closer to home, a disturbance moving over the 
top of the ridge is spreading mid and high level clouds over Lake 
Superior, with even a few weak radar echos noted near Isle Royale 
today. Otherwise, lingering surface high pressure is promoting 
another pleasant day with light winds and sunny skies across most of 
the UP, with temperatures again rising into the upper 70s to low 80s 
as of mid afternoon. Strong mixing has allowed dewpoints to fall 
into the upper 40s to low 50s across the west, supporting RH values 
dipping near or below 30% in a few locations. Despite that, do not 
expect any major fire weather concerns with winds mostly remaining 
below 15 mph this afternoon and RH quickly recovering tonight. 

More active weather is on tap for the next couple of days as the 
central CONUS ridge is progressively flattened out by the deep Pac 
NW trough lifting into the Canadian Prairie provinces. This is 
inducing surface cyclogenesis in the lee of the northern Rockies 
today, with the resultant strong low then forecast to track to the 
southern shores of Hudson Bay by Wednesday morning and driving a 
series of fronts across the UP tonight through early Wednesday.

A warm front will push into the western UP late tonight accompanied 
by deep moisture as PWATs climb to 1.75-2.00", bringing a round of 
showers and thunderstorms to the area through Tuesday. Expect most 
of the area to receive a wetting rainfall from this system as the 
NBM continues to depict a 65% or greater chance to receive at least 
a quarter inch for all but the far southcentral UP (closer to 50%) 
through Tuesday night. The western UP from the Keweenaw to the 
Porcupines still shows a roughly 40-60% chance to receive an inch or 
more of rain on Tuesday, but those probabilities quickly drop off to 
15-30% over the central and eastern UP. SPC continues to highlight a 
Day 2 marginal risk for severe weather over the western half of the 
UP given MUCAPE of 500+ J/kg and bulk shear values increasing above 
40 kt. That said, we remain rather pessimistic on overall 
strong/severe potential for Tuesday as the most favorable 
instability will not materialize until well after the best forcing 
has departed with the warm front. Additionally, model soundings 
continue to depict a strong capping inversion which will further 
inhibit any convective development. Any lingering shower and 
thunderstorm activity should depart the eastern UP behind the 
trailing cold front by Wednesday morning. 

Shifting gears to the expected breezy conditions through the middle 
of the week, southerly winds increase to 15-25 mph across a wide 
swath of the area tonight into Tuesday with the arrival of the warm 
front. The strongest gusts in this southerly warm advection regime 
will be in the areas favored by southerly downslope flow, 
particularly from the Huron Mountains eastward along the Lake 
Superior shoreline. These areas show a 60-70% chance for wind gusts 
of 35+ mph through Tuesday evening per latest HREF and NBM guidance.
Winds shift westerly and strengthen further on Wednesday, aided by 
cold air advection and pressure rises behind the cold front. Expect 
widespread gusts of 20-30 mph through the day, with NBM 
probabilities now increasing to 30-60% for gusts to 40 mph near Lake 
Superior. A Wind Advisory for the Keweenaw continues to look like a 
strong consideration as the NBM probability for gusts of 45+ mph has 
increased to 70-90%. Meanwhile, will also have to watch areas to the 
east as there is a 25-40% probability for 45 mph gusts along the 
shoreline from east of Marquette to Whitefish Point.

Expect calmer weather to return to the region by Thursday as high 
pressure temporarily builds back over the UP behind the departing 
system, with highs on Thursday closer to seasonal norms in the mid 
60s to low 70s. However, the overall pattern remains unsettled as 
another trough has the potential to bring additional rounds of 
precipitation and breezy conditions into the weekend.
